subject: Modeling binary, longitudinal data with missing values

messages.author: 7f3dcb786c576e61
messages.subject: Modeling binary, longitudinal data with missing values
parts:
Thanks for Stan, so very useful and powerful.

I have binary outcomes for a large number of items (I1-I3 in example below) over a number of time-ordered sessions (S1-S4 below). For each session there is only partial information, i.e. outcomes for some items are missing. In typical use cases the number of items are in the thousands and the number of items are in the range 50-1000.

Example:

Item,S1,S2,S3,S4
I1,0,1,X,0
I2,1,1,0,0
I3,X,0,0,0

For each item I want to predict the probability of getting an outcome of 1 in the next session. It is reasonable to assume there is both long-term and short-term trends, i.e. items that have had many 1's overall are more likely to have 1 in next session, and items that recently had many 1's is more likely to have a 1 in next session. It is also reasonable to assume that the items are clustered/grouped where items in a cluster/group behave similarly. This clustering can, at least as a first approximation, be assumed to be static, i.e. not change over time.

I have been thinking of some kind of logistic regression combined with ARIMA combined with some indian/chinese buffet process for the clustering but I'd appreciate pointers to papers/models or even Stan code that is relevant for my case.

Thanks in advance, Robert Feldt

This doesn't look too difficult. You should be able to marginalize out the discrete, unknown parameter directly. See the manual for how to do this -- it's going to be much better than me trying to describe it to you.

I have been thinking of some kind of logistic regression combined with ARIMA combined with some indian/chinese buffet process for the clustering but I'd appreciate pointers to papers/models or even Stan code that is relevant for my case.

I don't understand your model based on your description of the data and what you've described as the outcome. What are you trying to cluster? Have you tried formulating a model?

I think the next step would be to actually build a simple Stan model to start. I think what you're describing can be done, but that's just a guess. There should be an ARIMA model in our example-models repo: http://github.com/stan-dev/example-models. You can't express a truly non-parameteric model in Stan, but you can express a truncated one. Even so, you'll have a non-identifiability issue if you're not careful about your model.

 
Next steps:
- build a Stan program that ingests the data
- add to that a simple model clearly indicating the parameters you're trying to do inference over (that might explain what you're trying to do with clustering)
- get back to us




Daniel
Thanks in advance, Robert Feldt
